title: Taipei 101 Hides a 660-Ton Steel Ball to Stop Sway

scenes.text: Inside a Taipei skyscraper hangs a 660-ton steel ball.
It is a giant pendulum, hung between the 87th and 91st floors.
When typhoon winds push the tower one way, the ball swings the other.
In 2015 it swung about three feet during Typhoon Soudelor.
It cuts the swaying of the tower by up to forty percent.
A giant ball keeping a skyscraper standing.

description:
Taipei 101 has a 660-ton steel pendulum hanging between the 87th and 92nd floors.
It swings against the wind to reduce the building's sway, and in 2015 it moved about three feet during Typhoon Soudelor.
Would you stand under it?
first_comment: The damper is about 18 feet across and made of 41 layers of steel plates. Would you work on a floor that high?
